original_question: Classify Proper Holomorphic Correspondences from the unit disc to itself.
target_in_paper: Closest identifiable paper-faithful target: the unnumbered open-problem-list entry in arXiv:math/9509202 concerning the classification of proper holomorphic correspondences of the unit disc with itself.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main object (proper holomorphic correspondences), the source and target (the unit disc to itself), and the intended task (classification rather than a broader mapping or extension problem).
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated explicitly: everything is over the complex numbers.
The unit disc should be defined explicitly, e.g. D = {z in C : |z| < 1}.
"Proper holomorphic correspondence" should be defined stand-alone, not left implicit.
A precise formulation should specify the correspondence as a pure one-dimensional complex-analytic subset Gamma of D x D.
One should state the projection condition explicitly: the first coordinate projection pi_1|_Gamma : Gamma -> D is surjective and proper.
In this setting, it is helpful to make explicit the equivalent boundary formulation Gamma intersect (D x partial D) = empty set.
The draft does not say whether reducible correspondences are included, or whether classification is first up to irreducible components.
The draft does not make explicit that branched/multivalued correspondences are allowed, so that the problem is not misread as classifying only single-valued self-maps f : D -> D.

The draft does not specify what counts as a classification: a description of all such analytic subsets Gamma subset D x D, rather than only a list of examples or only classification up to automorphism.
If one wants the geometric language often used in this subject, one may need to note the bidisc picture: pure one-dimensional analytic subsets of D^2 with boundary in T^2, where T = partial D.
refined_question: Classify all proper holomorphic correspondences from the unit disc D = {z in C : |z| < 1} to itself; that is, describe all pure one-dimensional complex-analytic subsets Gamma subset D x D such that the first coordinate projection pi_1|_Gamma : Gamma -> D is surjective and proper (equivalently, Gamma intersect (D x partial D) = empty set), allowing multivalued and branched correspondences and not restricting to single-valued proper self-maps of D.
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is a problem list rather than a theorem paper, and its abstract states that it collects open problems in several complex variables and related areas. Because the web-accessible arXiv landing page exposes only the abstract and not the full list entry itself, the sharpest recoverable paper-faithful refinement is the classification problem your draft already points to, but rewritten with the standard SCV definition of a proper holomorphic correspondence. The external SCV sources consulted make precise the notion used here: a proper holomorphic correspondence from D to D is a pure one-dimensional analytic subset of D x D with proper first projection, equivalently one avoiding D x partial D; and this is the same geometric class as pure one-dimensional analytic subvarieties of the bidisc whose boundary lies in the torus. So the rewrite stays as close as possible to your draft while adding the missing analytic-set, projection, boundary, and multivaluedness data needed to make it stand alone.
